chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abu Khalid, who said:

Wash everything from the deceased who drowned, and the one eaten by the predatory wild animals, and everything except the one who was killed between the two swords. So if he had a remnant of life (breath), he would be washed, otherwise, no.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing the dead who drowned or were eaten by animals?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the ritual purification (*ghusl*) for martyrs and specific deaths, distinguishing between those who died instantly in combat versus those who retained a remnant of life (*ramaq*). It establishes that while most non-martyr deaths like drowning or predation require washing, instantaneous battlefield death exempts the body from this specific ritual, reflecting the high status of the martyr. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the treatment of the deceased in various circumstances of death.
